title: Another attempt at creating combat animations with Seedance 2.0 after countless failed attempts with ChatGPT
author: Longjumping_Wall9861
selftext:
Couple of weeks ago I posted here my results after starting using Seedance 2.0 instead of ChatGPT to generate combat animations. I kept working on it and decided to split the combat animations into a hit-hit summon giant object from top mechanic and wanted to share out the results with you.

  
**1. Start frame.** One painted still of the character in its ready pose, made with ChatGPT image, on pure green at 1280x720 with the feet on a fixed row. That single image is the only input. I had these sprites since the beginning of the game that I also generated from the equipment images.

**2. Attack video.** Seedance 2.0 in Dreamina, “First and last frames” mode with the last frame left empty, 720p, 4 seconds is enough and costs less. Omni reference mode redrew the character at a different scale and added odd extra slashes, so we don’t use it. The prompt describes every cut by the character’s own hands and by both sides of the image (“his right to his left, image left to right”), because “slash to the left” came out backwards so you need to tell left according to where.

**4. Cutting.** A small tool I built with Opus loads the clip, keys out the green and lets us pick frames one by one. I adjust the timings of the hits by adjusting the number of frames they get. Each frame is played same amount of time o i give first hit 5-7 frames, second hit a bit less 4-6 frames then last 15 frames are mostly spent on gathering energy with sword raised then the sword becomes normal and character returns to normal in 2-3 frames. Total 30 frames per attack animation.

**5. In game.** Every frame plays for the same time. A mimic that dies in one hit plays one attack, two hits play attacks 1 and 2, and three hits play the whole combo. Damage numbers wait for the marked contact frame. In the sprite tool I mark start,end and hit frames of attack 1,2,3 so that the game can now which frames to play for each attack and when to show the hit VFX and damage numbers..

**6. Finishers.** The big object on the last hit (the hammer for Cloisonné Court, the sword for Porcelain Dancer) is not in the video generated by Seedance. Enemy distance can vary so the falling object must be generated seperately. I use ChatGPT to generate these objects. Then they start free falling from above, slow down before the combat and get a bit transparent as they start contacting the monster. Upon hit I added some VFX that I saw from a developer on Instagram: a ground ripple, a flash, debris and a squash on the enemy and then the object slowly fades away.

Last time I posted here, someone noticed the sword becoming a simitar like object just in 1 frame that plays for like 30ms in a 30 frame animation so I wonder what slop will people find out now in this clip but I also received some nice messages and people asking me how to do animations like it so I'm glad if it helps anyone in their game development journey

The game is called Mimic2 - Idle MMORPG. It is coming to steam on 28th of October. Feel free to add to wishlist or if you want to try out the beta you can play from browser or Google Play now.

comments.author: nexuscoregaming
comments.body: Crazy improvement, I’ve been having issues with ChatGPT as well. Will have to give Seedance a shot.

replies.author: Longjumping_Wall9861
replies.body: I would definitely suggest it. I tried lots of different things but none of them create reliable sprites.

comments.author: iamthelobo
comments.body: This looks good. I think a good next milestone would be to add deliberate holds and some anticipation to the animations to make the attacks have more impact. There is a really good skullgirls design doc that you can have your agent read and add to your animation md file. Here it is: [https://media.gdcvault.com/gdcchina14/presentations/833784\_MarielCartwright\_PowerfulAndEffective\_EN.pdf](https://media.gdcvault.com/gdcchina14/presentations/833784_MarielCartwright_PowerfulAndEffective_EN.pdf)
